title: CONVEY Act
official_summary:
Clifton Opportunities Now for Vibrant Economic Yields Act or the CONVEY Act

This act directs the Bureau of Land Management to convey to Mesa County, Colorado, a parcel of land in Clifton for fair market value.

The county must pay all costs associated with the conveyance, including any surveying costs.

The proceeds from the conveyance must be deposited into the Federal Land Disposal Account and be available for expenditure.

summary.headline: Law requires the federal government to sell a parcel of public land in Clifton, Colorado, to Mesa County at fair market value.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Bureau of Land Management to transfer a piece of federal land in Clifton, Colorado, to Mesa County. The county must pay fair market value for the land and cover all costs of the transfer, including surveying. The money from the sale goes into a federal fund called the Federal Land Disposal Account, where it can be spent.

who_it_affects.how: The county gains ownership of the land but must pay its fair market value plus all transfer and survey costs.
Land in their community moves from federal to county control.
The agency must carry out the transfer and gives up management of the parcel.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the summary does not give a deadline for completing the transfer.
